name: Mushroom brown
lede: Mushroom brown is a light, grayish reddish brown charted by Ridgway in 1912 and matched closely, 2.1 units, by the ISCC-NBS system in 1955, a block that at least ten other twentieth-century trade names also claimed.

sections.title: One block, a dozen names
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature lists this tone, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 places it in block 45 with a close 2.1-unit fit [1]. In the ColorHub library the same point is also carried under Brownish Drab, an exact duplicate (ΔE 0.0), and the same block attracted a run of other twentieth-century trade names, among them Buckskin, Deauville Sand, Autumn Blonde and French Nude [1][3]. No book held in color-kb discusses "Mushroom brown" itself [4].

Its nearest distinct neighbor is [[beaver]], 3.4 units off, "almost the same" by our graph, with [[taupe]] close by at 4.2 [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds Mushroom brown in 1,079 of 23,781 paintings, about 4.5 percent, one of the more common tones in this group, as photographed [2]. It appears across very different traditions: a Ming-dynasty Chinese scroll by Xu Ben, a seventeenth-century Japanese landscape by Iwasa Matabei, and a Redon panel, each with Mushroom brown covering most of the canvas [2]. Counts are computed matches on varnished, photographed paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
